title: By spirit and by species; these two grades may be called intellectual
pass_a_gloss: XVI. By spirit, which teaching the intellect speaks within or without. Examples see Acts 8:29 and chapter 16:7. XVII. By species, by which it immediately changes the mind opened from the senses by a perfect ecstasy. Paul the Apostle sets forth an illustrious example, 2 Corinthians 12:2. Compare our epilogism on the true religion and the Catholic Church, disputation 10 on prophetic light, page 207, and disputation 12 on divine prophecy, page 205 and following. But these two grades can be comprehended under one, which we shall not inconveniently call intellectual.
pass_b_english: XVI. By spirit: speaking within or without, it teaches the intellect. For examples see [[Acts 8:29 >> Bible:Acts 8:29]] and [[Acts 16:7 >> Bible:Acts 16:7]].

XVII. By species: it immediately transforms the mind once a perfect ecstasy has opened that mind and withdrawn it from the senses. Paul the Apostle supplies a famous instance ([[2 Corinthians 12:2 >> Bible:2 Corinthians 12:2]]). Compare our epilogism On the true religion and the Catholic Church, disputation 10 on prophetic light, page 207, and disputation 12 on divine prophecy, page 205 and following. These two grades can be gathered under one name; we may without inconvenience call it intellectual.
source_text:
XVI. Per spiritum, qui intus aut foris loquendo intellectum docet.
Exempla vide Act. 8. v. 29. & cap. 16. v. 7.

XVII. Per speciem, qua mentem a sensibus perfecta ecstasi apertam immediate immutat.
Illustre exemplum exhibet Paulus Apostolus 2. Cor. 12. v. 2. Confer epilogismum nostrum de vera religione & Catholica Ecclesia disp. 10. de lumine prophetico, pag. 207. & disputationem 12. de vaticinio divino, pag. 205. & seqq. Hi autem duo gradus sub uno comprehendi possunt, quem intellectualem non incommode dicemus.
